chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Sa'id al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It is necessary for the first-timer (al-sarura) to enter the House before he returns.
So when you enter it, enter it with tranquility and dignity.
Then go to every one of its corners.
Then say: 'O Allah, indeed You said, "And whoever enters it shall be secure," so secure me from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection.'
And pray between the two pillars that are adjacent to the red marble slab.
And if the people are numerous, face each corner from your place where you prayed.
And supplicate to Allah and ask Him.

key_terms.الرُّخَامَة الْحَمْرَاء: The red marble slab (in the Kaaba)
key_terms.الصَّرُورَة: The first-time visitor to the Kaaba

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended etiquettes and rituals for a first-time visitor entering the Kaaba according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific Sunnah for a first-time pilgrim (al-sarura), emphasizing entering with tranquility (sakinah) and reciting a supplication that links physical safety to spiritual security from the Hereafter. It prescribes praying between the two pillars adjacent to the Black Stone (Rukn al-Yamani and Rukn al-Shami), a practice rooted in the Prophet’s tradition, while offering practical flexibility for crowded conditions by directing the pilgrim to face each corner individually.
